title: SpanGate: async-aware instrumentation and adaptive sampling middleware
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Implement an SDK middleware and runtime hook (SpanGate) that reduces tracing overhead for high-throughput paths while preserving fidelity for debugging. SpanGate is an adaptive gatekeeper that decides whether to create full spans, lightweight spans, or to skip instrumentation based on: request priority, sampled token, recent error rate, KV-baggage size, and current token budget. It must be async-aware (propagate decisions across fibers/promises) and provide a low-allocation fast-path for hot code paths.
acceptance_criteria: SpanGate middleware added to Node, Go, and Python SDKs with consistent config schema
Adaptive sampling config supports static rate, error-rate driven boosts, and explicit force-sample header
Context propagation token (span_gate_token) flows across async boundaries and across service-to-service via a compact header
CPU overhead for non-sampled requests reduced by >= 40% compared to current SDK baseline (measured on 1ms median handler)
Integration tests that validate decision continuity across promise/async/worker boundaries
Canary rollout plan documented and feature-flagged with opt-out for customers

2025-02-02 - QA Lead: Integration harness ready. Observed sporadic decision flips in long-lived HTTP/2 streams; suspected clock skew affecting error-rate window. Added mitigation to use sliding counters with monotonic clock.

notes: Design trade-offs: prefer compact token with conservative heuristics to avoid cross-service divergence. Alternative (rejected): full distributed coordinator for sampling decisions due to added latency. The token should be readable without expensive parsing; use bitfields for flags and a 16-bit sampling-stability counter.
